column1: # Shared instant-cache key vectors for the Unix path -> cache-key encoder and
# its on-disk chunking. Read by the Rust test
# Format: one vector per line, tab-separated: input<TAB>expected<TAB>stem.
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. Extra columns after
# `stem` are reserved for future vectors and MUST be ignored by readers that do
# not know them. No column may be empty.
# `input` uses the mini escape scheme of json_escape_vectors.tsv --
# backslash first: \\ -> one literal backslash byte, \n -> LF, \r -> CR,
# \t -> tab -- plus \xHH -> the byte HH, for input that is not UTF-8.
# `expected` is literal (the Unix key never contains a backslash, tab or
# Unix scheme, over the path's bytes: _->__ /->_s \->_b :->_c space->_w, an
# ASCII capital -> _u and its lowercase letter, and every byte of a non-ASCII
# character or of a sequence that is not UTF-8 -> _x and two lowercase hex
# digits. Every other byte, including the Windows-reserved ? * < > " |,
# passes through unchanged. A key is therefore lowercase ASCII: roots that
# differ only in case, Unicode normalization or invalid bytes never share a
# file on a volume that folds them. Every reader MUST fail if this file is
# `stem` is the cache file's path relative to the instant-prompts
# directory, minus its `.{suffix}.{token}.{ext}` tail: the key itself when it
# is at most 200 bytes, else the key split into 50-byte chunks joined by `/`
# (every chunk but the last is a directory). Each reader asserts the relative
# path `{stem}.git.none.{ext}` its builder produces. Rows over 200 bytes
